::: {.lead-copy}
I am a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Biostatistics in the Department of Population Health Sciences at Georgia State University’s School of Public Health. My research interests include survey methodology, causal inference, longitudinal data analysis and study design, and life course and aging research.

I am interested in addressing the data and methodological challenges involved in understanding how early- and midlife experiences and social determinants shape later-life cognitive aging. I am enthusiastic about integrating different types of data to answer meaningful research questions, while accounting for differences in population representation and measurement across sources.

Before joining Georgia State University, I completed postdoctoral training in biostatistics at Duke University. I received my doctoral and master’s training in the Program in Survey and Data Science at the University of Michigan.
